# Drop the sandbox module and leave sandboxes to the platform that runs them

## Intent

AgentKit stops creating and managing sandboxes itself. Isolation, lifetime,
credentials and file transfer belong to the platform that owns the sandbox
(Parley on OpenShell), and AgentKit supplies only the hands that work in it.
The repository drops its sandbox module, its gateway, its sandbox image and
their examples, and a pinned consumer can still reach the last release that
had them.

## Goals

1. The repository holds no `sandbox/` tree, no gateway, no sandbox image and
   no `examples/sandbox`, `examples/gateway` or `examples/harness`, and no
   sandbox, gateway, container or `proto` make target.
2. No `go.mod` of the repository requires `github.com/gokrazy/rsync` or
   `github.com/landlock-lsm/go-landlock` at all, or `google.golang.org/grpc`
   or `google.golang.org/protobuf` directly.
3. `make check` passes over the modules that remain: the root, `codesearch`,
   `mcpserve` and `examples/indexedsearch`.
4. The last commit that still has the sandbox is the release `v0.9.1`,
   reachable by its root, `codesearch/`, `sandbox/` and `mcpserve/` tags, and
   `docs/releasing.md` names it.
5. Every reference doc, README, generated doc and doc comment says what is
   true after the removal, and a new ADR records the decision, superseding
   ADR 05 and ADR 06.

## Non-goals

- The `agentkit-tools` command: the tool set and its flags, the MCP session
  mode, the single-call mode, the `tools` listing, the example that replaces
  `examples/harness`, and its `docs/cli.md` section. This is the second scope
  of PRD 15, its own package (`tool_server_command`).
- The index that outlives the process: `--index-dir`,
  `AGENTKIT_INDEX_DIR`, reuse across processes and `find_symbol` from the
  stored index. This is the third scope of PRD 15, its own package
  (`persistent_code_index`).
- Any change under `.github/workflows`, including
  `build-sandbox-containers.yaml` and the reusable `inc-build.yaml`
  (owner's decision, Design Decision 4).
- Creating, isolating, listing or destroying sandboxes, and moving files in
  or out of one. Parley does this (its PRD §13).
- Confining `execute` on a host without a sandbox. After this package the
  shell guard is again the only boundary there, as before PRD 11.
- Creating or pushing the `v0.9.1` tags. The owner does it before the
  removal is implemented (Design Decision 2).
- Moving spec 25 or any other package to `superseded`. That is a lifecycle
  move of those packages, made by their owner.
- Changes to `mcpserve`'s API, to the tool definitions, to code mode, or to
  `codesearch`.
- `hack/rmi-untagged-images.sh`, a generic helper that removes untagged
  Podman images; it is not part of the sandbox and stays.

## Background

AgentKit has its own sandboxes (PRD 11, specs 13 to 19 and 25): the
`sandbox` module (`sandbox/go.mod`) with the `agentkit-sandboxd` agent
(`sandbox/cmd/agentkit-sandboxd`) and its gRPC protocol
(`sandbox/internal/sandboxpb`), proxy tools, an rsync-based sync and export
(`sandbox/internal/rsyncx`), the Podman, Landlock, local and gateway
providers (`sandbox/podman`, `sandbox/landlock`, `sandbox/local`,
`sandbox/gateway`), the `sandbox/gatewayd` module with `agentkit-gateway`,
and the `containers/agentkit-sandbox` image. It is about 15 000 lines of
production Go and as many of tests. Inside the repository only
`examples/sandbox`, `examples/gateway` and `examples/harness` import it; the
project owner confirmed nothing outside does.

Parley now owns sandboxes for the agent-fox projects. A Parley sandbox is an
OpenShell sandbox born with a fork checked out, with Parley's credentials,
network policy, quotas and checkpoints. The planned OpenShell provider of
PRD 11 was never built, and with Parley it has no purpose. The decision rule
of PRD 10 applies: is this here because the model is bad at judgment, or
because we chose to own the whole stack? The tools are the first kind.
Sandboxes, once Parley exists, are the second.

What the removal touches outside the deleted trees, as the repository stands:

- The `Makefile`: `MODULES` lists `sandbox`, `sandbox/gatewayd`,
  `examples/sandbox`, `examples/gateway` and `examples/harness`; `doc` loops
  over `sandbox` and `sandbox/gatewayd`; `LDFLAGS` stamps
  `sandbox/internal/buildver`, and nothing reads `LDFLAGS`, `VERSION`,
  `COMMIT` or `BUILD_TIME` but it and the removed targets; the variables
  `CONTAINER_REGISTRY`,
  `SANDBOX_IMAGE`, `SANDBOX_IMAGE_TAG`, `SANDBOX_TEST_ENV`,
  `AGENTKIT_SANDBOX_GIT_URL`, `PROTO_DIR`, `PROTOC_GEN_GO` and
  `PROTOC_GEN_GO_GRPC`; the targets `proto`, `build-containers`,
  `build-sandbox-container`, `sandbox-podman-test`, `sandbox-landlock-test`,
  `sandbox-gateway` and `sandbox-gateway-test`.
- `internal/policy/builds_test.go` reads `MODULES` from the `Makefile` and
  builds and vets every module for four targets and the host
  (`TestCrossTargetBuildAndVet`, `TestHostCgoBuildAndVet`; slow, skipped
  under `-short`).
- Test helpers only the sandbox uses: `testutil.Tar` in
  `internal/testutil/testutil.go` (with `TestTarHoldsTheFilesInNameOrder`)
  and `Tree.Tar` in `internal/toolconformance/toolconformance.go`.
- `.dockerignore`, which exists for the sandbox image's build context, and
  the `/agentkit-sandboxd` line of `.gitignore`.
- Doc comments that describe sandbox behaviour: `workspace/workspace.go`,
  `guard/guard.go`, `mcpserve/doc.go`, `mcpserve/buildinfo.go`, the comment
  of `mcpserve/go.mod`, `internal/toolconformance/toolconformance.go` and
  `tools/for_test.go`. (`examples/codingagent/main.go` and `codemode` use
  "sandbox" in its general sense and stay as they are.)
- Docs: `README.md`, `examples/README.md`, `examples/codingagent/README.md`,
  `docs/DEPS.md`, `docs/cli.md`, `docs/api.md`, `docs/architecture.md`,
  `docs/guide.md`, `docs/configuration.md`, `docs/development.md`,
  `docs/releasing.md` and `docs/generated/` (`docs/generated/sandbox/`, and
  the comments that `make doc` copies into the generated docs of `guard`,
  `workspace`, `codemode` and `mcpserve`).
- ADR 05 (`docs/adr/05-keep-the-sandbox-in-its-own-module-and-sync-through-a-filtered-view.md`)
  and ADR 06 (`docs/adr/06-authenticate-every-gateway-rpc-before-reading-it.md`),
  both `Status: Accepted`.
- The release tags on origin are `v0.9.0` and `codesearch/v0.9.0`; `sandbox/`
  and `mcpserve/` have never been tagged, so no consumer can pin the sandbox
  module today.

## Requirements

### The last release with sandboxes

Before the removal, the owner runs `make check-release` on `main` and tags
the commit the removal starts from as the release `v0.9.1`: `v0.9.1`,
`codesearch/v0.9.1`, `sandbox/v0.9.1` and `mcpserve/v0.9.1`, all on that one
commit, pushed to origin. The implementer does not create them. They check
that all four exist and point at the commit the removal branch starts from,
and they stop before deleting anything if any is missing or points elsewhere,
naming each such tag.

After the removal, `docs/releasing.md` names `v0.9.1` as the last release
with sandboxes and says that `sandbox/v0.9.1` is the version to pin for them.
Its release steps tag the root, `codesearch/` and `mcpserve/` modules, and
it describes no image and no gateway.

### Removing the code and the modules

The repository holds none of: the `sandbox` module and its providers, agent,
protocols and internal packages; `sandbox/gatewayd` and `agentkit-gateway`;
`containers/agentkit-sandbox`; `examples/sandbox`, `examples/gateway` and
`examples/harness`; `.dockerignore`; the `/agentkit-sandboxd` line of
`.gitignore`; the test helpers only the removed code used.

- `MODULES` lists exactly `.`, `codesearch`, `mcpserve` and
  `examples/indexedsearch`, and every one of them builds and vets for every
  cross target and the host.
- No `go.mod` requires `github.com/gokrazy/rsync` or
  `github.com/landlock-lsm/go-landlock`, and `go list -m all` in no module
  lists them. No `go.mod` requires `google.golang.org/grpc` or
  `google.golang.org/protobuf` without `// indirect`: they stay in the graphs
  of the root and `mcpserve` (through the Vertex AI dependencies) and of
  `codesearch` (through zoekt).
- `make tidy` leaves every `go.mod` and `go.sum` as committed.

### Build tooling

- The `Makefile` defines none of the targets and variables listed in the
  background; `make help` lists no target that names a sandbox, the gateway,
  a container or `proto`, and `make proto` fails as an unknown target.
- `make doc` documents the root, `codesearch` and `mcpserve` modules only;
  `docs/generated/` holds no `sandbox/` directory, and a second run leaves
  it unchanged.
- No file under `.github/workflows` changes.
- `make check` exits 0.

### Docs and doc comments

- The reference docs and READMEs listed in the background describe no
  sandbox module, provider, agent, gateway, sandbox image or `proto` target
  as part of AgentKit: none of the names `agentkit-sandboxd`,
  `agentkit-gateway`, `gatewayd`, `sandbox/` as a path of this repository,
  `sandbox.` as a Go identifier, `podman` or `landlock` appears in them,
  except in `docs/releasing.md`'s statement of the last release with
  sandboxes. Each one's **Contents** index matches its headings. The word
  "sandbox" in its general sense ("the guard is a floor, not a sandbox",
  "a sandbox someone else runs") stays.
- `docs/DEPS.md` drops the rulings and allowlist rows of
  `google.golang.org/grpc`, `google.golang.org/protobuf`,
  `github.com/gokrazy/rsync` and `github.com/landlock-lsm/go-landlock`, and
  no longer says the list covers the `sandbox` or `sandbox/gatewayd` module.
- `docs/cli.md` stays and says in one line that the repository ships no
  command-line program; the `agentkit-tools` package adds its section.
- The doc comments listed in the background say what is true afterwards and
  name no identifier, package or command of the removed module; the guard's
  comments say the guard is the only boundary on a host without a sandbox,
  and that `guard.AllowAll` fits a process already inside an isolation
  boundary someone else owns. `docs/generated/` is regenerated from them.
- Archived records (`docs/prd/`, `docs/archive/`, `.specs/`) are not
  rewritten.

### The decision record

- A new ADR, `docs/adr/08-leave-sandboxes-to-the-platform-that-runs-them.md`,
  `Status: Accepted`, records the decision: the sandbox module is deleted
  whole, why (Parley owns sandboxes; the PRD 10 rule), and the consequences
  (the shell guard is the only boundary on a bare host, `v0.9.1` is the last
  release with sandboxes, `examples/harness` is gone until `agentkit-tools`
  replaces it, the workflow left under `.github/workflows`).
- ADR 05 and ADR 06 keep their bodies; their status line reads that each is
  superseded by ADR 08, with a link. Neither is deleted.

### End-to-end flows

1. **A maintainer checks the tree after the removal.** The maintainer runs
   `make check` at the root: fmt, vet, lint and the short tests run in the
   four remaining modules and pass. `make doc` and `make tidy` change
   nothing. `make help` lists no removed target. No removed tree is tracked
   and no `go.mod` names rsync or go-landlock.
2. **A pinned consumer finds the last release with sandboxes.** A consumer
   reads `docs/releasing.md`, finds `v0.9.1`, and resolves `sandbox/v0.9.1`
   with git: the tagged tree holds `sandbox/go.mod`, and the tag sits on the
   commit the removal follows.

## Design Decisions

1. **Delete the sandbox module whole, in one cut** (owner's decision, PRD 15
   D1). Nothing outside the repository uses it and confined local runs are
   not needed. No Landlock library is kept.
2. **The last build with sandboxes is the ordinary release `v0.9.1`, and the
   owner tags it** (owner's decision, this run). Releasing needs
   `make check-release`, which agents never run, so the owner runs it on
   `main` and pushes `v0.9.1`, `codesearch/v0.9.1`, `sandbox/v0.9.1` and
   `mcpserve/v0.9.1` before the removal is implemented. A patch version,
   because nothing since `v0.9.0` changed the API. Go resolves nested modules
   only from version tags, so a pinned consumer needs `sandbox/v0.9.1`.
3. **The removal lands first of PRD 15's three scopes** (owner's decision,
   this run). `examples/harness` is deleted before its replacement exists;
   the replacement example and the `docs/cli.md` section of `agentkit-tools`
   land with the `tool_server_command` package.
4. **Nothing under `.github/workflows` changes** (owner's decision, this run),
   overriding PRD 15's removal of the image's publishing workflow.
   `build-sandbox-containers.yaml` starts on every push to `main` and builds
   `containers/agentkit-sandbox/Containerfile`, which this package deletes, so
   that workflow fails until the owner changes it.
5. **"No gRPC or protobuf requirement" means no direct one** (decided from
   the code). `google.golang.org/grpc` and `google.golang.org/protobuf` are
   indirect requirements of the root and `mcpserve` (Vertex AI) and of
   `codesearch` (zoekt), which no removal can change. rsync and go-landlock
   leave every module graph.
6. **Test helpers that only the removed code used go with it** (decided from
   the code): `testutil.Tar` with its test, and `toolconformance`'s
   `Tree.Tar`. `toolconformance` stays: `tools` runs its case table.
7. **`.dockerignore` and the `/agentkit-sandboxd` ignore line go** (decided
   from the code): both exist only for the deleted image and binary.
8. **`docs/cli.md` stays with one line** (steering): a repository without a
   CLI keeps the file and says it has none, until `agentkit-tools` arrives.
9. **Profile: full.** The removal is verified end to end by the maintainer's
   `make check` and the consumer's tag lookup, which the integration task
   runs.
10. **The package lists specs 13 to 19 and 25 in `supersedes`**, whose code
    it removes. Changing their status is a separate lifecycle move by their
    owner.

## Dependencies

- PRD 15 (`docs/prd/15-serve-the-tools-from-one-command-and-drop-the-sandbox.md`):
  the source; this package is its first scope.
- PRD 11 (`docs/prd/11-run-tools-in-an-isolated-sandbox.md`) and PRD 13
  (`docs/prd/13-authenticate-gateway-tokens-with-a-callback.md`): superseded.
- Spec 25 `gateway_authenticator` (active, all tasks done): its code is
  removed. Archived specs 13 to 19: their code is removed.
- ADR 05 and ADR 06: superseded by ADR 08, which this package writes.
- Parley (`github.com/agent-fox-dev/parley`, PRD §13): the platform that owns
  sandboxes from now on.

## Glossary

- **The removal**: the change this package makes, on the branch that starts
  from the commit tagged `v0.9.1`.
- **The last release with sandboxes**: `v0.9.1`, with its `codesearch/`,
  `sandbox/` and `mcpserve/` tags on the same commit.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: The last release with sandboxes

**Rationale:** Go resolves a nested module only from a version tag, so a consumer pinned to the sandbox module needs one on the last commit that has it.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] THE release SHALL carry the four tags v0.9.1, codesearch/v0.9.1, sandbox/v0.9.1 and mcpserve/v0.9.1, all on the commit the removal branch starts from, whose tree still holds sandbox/go.mod
   → for each of the four tags, `git rev-parse <tag>^{commit}` prints the removal's base commit; `git ls-tree --name-only sandbox/v0.9.1 -- sandbox/go.mod` prints sandbox/go.mod
   Check: same as PATH-2
1. [REQ-1.2] THE docs/releasing.md SHALL name v0.9.1 as the last release with sandboxes and sandbox/v0.9.1 as the version to pin for them, give the root, codesearch/ and mcpserve/ tags as the tags of a release, and describe no image and no gateway
   → the file holds sandbox/v0.9.1 in its statement of the last release with sandboxes; its tag commands name v<X>, codesearch/v<X> and mcpserve/v<X> and no sandbox/ tag; it has no section on an image, its workflow, its tags, its registry secrets, building it, or the gateway
   Check: same as PATH-2

### REQ-2: Sandbox code and modules removed

**Rationale:** Parley owns sandboxes now; code nobody uses is code someone still has to build, test and keep in step.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] THE repository SHALL track no file under sandbox/, containers/agentkit-sandbox/, examples/sandbox/, examples/gateway/ or examples/harness/, no .dockerignore, and no /agentkit-sandboxd line in .gitignore
   → `git ls-files sandbox containers/agentkit-sandbox examples/sandbox examples/gateway examples/harness .dockerignore` prints nothing; `grep -x /agentkit-sandboxd .gitignore` exits 1
   Check: same as PATH-1
1. [REQ-2.2] THE Makefile SHALL list exactly the modules ., codesearch, mcpserve and examples/indexedsearch in MODULES, each of which builds and vets for every cross target and for the host
   → the Makefile line reads `MODULES := . codesearch mcpserve examples/indexedsearch`; TestCrossTargetBuildAndVet and TestHostCgoBuildAndVet pass over those four modules
   Check: integration
   - setup: the go toolchain, with cross compilation for linux/amd64, linux/arm64, darwin/arm64 and windows/amd64
   - setup: go test run without -short, as make check-release runs it; that run is the owner's, not the implementer's
   ```
   in internal/policy/builds_test.go, unchanged: modules(t) reads the four directories from the Makefile's MODULES; TestCrossTargetBuildAndVet runs `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` in each for every cross target, TestHostCgoBuildAndVet for the host with cgo; both pass. Under -short (make check) both skip, so the implementer runs `go build ./... && go vet ./...` in each of the four modules and asserts exit 0
   ```
1. [REQ-2.3] THE repository SHALL for any go.mod in the repository, require neither github.com/gokrazy/rsync nor github.com/landlock-lsm/go-landlock, and require google.golang.org/grpc and google.golang.org/protobuf only as indirect requirements
   → `go list -m all` in each of the four modules lists neither github.com/gokrazy/rsync nor github.com/landlock-lsm/go-landlock; every line of every go.mod that names google.golang.org/grpc or google.golang.org/protobuf ends in `// indirect`
   Check: same as PATH-1
1. [REQ-2.4] WHEN make tidy runs on the removal tree, THE repository SHALL leave every go.mod and go.sum as committed
   → `git status --porcelain` prints nothing after `make tidy`
   Check: same as PATH-1
1. [REQ-2.5] THE internal test helpers SHALL keep no helper that only the removed code called, while toolconformance's case table stays and the tools package still runs it
   → testutil.Tar, its test TestTarHoldsTheFilesInNameOrder and toolconformance's Tree.Tar are gone and no Go file calls them; TestToolsConformToTheSharedCaseTable passes
   Check: unit
   ```
   in tools/for_test.go: TestToolsConformToTheSharedCaseTable, unchanged but for its comment, builds tools.For over each toolconformance tree and runs every case of toolconformance.CaseNames(); all pass. `go vet ./...` in the root module passes with the two Tar helpers deleted
   ```

### REQ-3: Build tooling without sandbox targets

**Rationale:** A make target or a generated doc for a module that no longer exists fails the first person who runs it.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-3.1] THE Makefile SHALL define none of the targets proto, build-containers, build-sandbox-container, sandbox-podman-test, sandbox-landlock-test, sandbox-gateway and sandbox-gateway-test, and none of the variables VERSION, COMMIT, BUILD_TIME, LDFLAGS, CONTAINER_REGISTRY, SANDBOX_IMAGE, SANDBOX_IMAGE_TAG, SANDBOX_TEST_ENV, AGENTKIT_SANDBOX_GIT_URL, PROTO_DIR, PROTOC_GEN_GO and PROTOC_GEN_GO_GRPC
   → `make help` lists none of those targets; `make proto` exits non-zero with make's `No rule to make target` message
   Check: same as PATH-1
1. [REQ-3.2] WHEN make doc runs, THE Makefile SHALL write the generated docs of the root, codesearch and mcpserve modules only
   → docs/generated/ holds no sandbox/ directory; after `make doc`, `git status --porcelain -- docs/generated` prints nothing
   Check: same as PATH-1
1. [REQ-3.3] THE repository SHALL for any file under .github/workflows, keep it byte-identical to the removal's base commit
   → `git diff --stat <base> -- .github/workflows` prints nothing
   Check: same as PATH-1
1. [REQ-3.4] WHEN make check runs at the root of the removal tree, THE Makefile SHALL run fmt, vet, lint and the short tests in each of the four remaining modules and pass
   → make check exits 0
   Check: same as PATH-1

### REQ-4: Docs and doc comments that say what is true

**Rationale:** Steering treats an outdated doc as a regression, and a doc that still promises sandboxes sends a reader to code that is gone.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-4.1] THE documentation SHALL describe no sandbox module, provider, agent, gateway, sandbox image or proto target as part of AgentKit in README.md, examples/README.md, examples/codingagent/README.md, docs/DEPS.md, docs/cli.md, docs/api.md, docs/architecture.md, docs/guide.md, docs/configuration.md, docs/development.md and docs/releasing.md, with each one's Contents index matching its headings
   → a case-insensitive search of those files for agentkit-sandboxd, agentkit-gateway, gatewayd, landlock, podman and `sandbox/`, and a case-sensitive one for a Go identifier of the sandbox package (`sandbox\.[A-Z]`), match only docs/releasing.md's statement of the last release with sandboxes; every Contents link in those files names a heading of the same file
   Check: same as PATH-1
1. [REQ-4.2] THE docs/DEPS.md SHALL hold no ruling and no allowlist row for google.golang.org/grpc, google.golang.org/protobuf, github.com/gokrazy/rsync or github.com/landlock-lsm/go-landlock, and name only the root and mcpserve modules as the modules its list covers
   → no heading and no allowlist row of docs/DEPS.md names any of the four modules; the paragraph after the allowlist names neither the sandbox nor the sandbox/gatewayd module
   Check: same as PATH-1
1. [REQ-4.3] THE docs/cli.md SHALL say in one line that the repository ships no command-line program, with no section on agentkit-sandboxd, agentkit-gateway or regenerating the protocols
   → the file holds its title and that one line, and no second-level heading
   Check: same as PATH-1
1. [REQ-4.4] THE Go doc comments SHALL name no identifier, package or command of the removed module in the comments of workspace/workspace.go, guard/guard.go, mcpserve/doc.go, mcpserve/buildinfo.go, mcpserve/go.mod, internal/toolconformance/toolconformance.go and tools/for_test.go, and say that the shell guard is the only boundary on a host without a sandbox and that guard.AllowAll fits a process already inside an isolation boundary someone else owns
   → those files match none of `sandbox\.[A-Z]` (a Go identifier of the sandbox package), `sandbox/`, IsolationContainer, IsolationMicroVM, NetworkNone, AgentInfo, agentkit-sandboxd and buildver; docs/generated/ equals the output of `make doc` over them
   Check: same as PATH-1

### REQ-5: The decision recorded in an ADR

**Rationale:** ADR 05 and ADR 06 describe rules for code that no longer exists; the reason it is gone belongs where the next reader looks for decisions.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-5.1] THE ADR record SHALL hold docs/adr/08-leave-sandboxes-to-the-platform-that-runs-them.md with status Accepted, recording that the sandbox module was deleted whole, why (Parley owns sandboxes; PRD 10's rule), and the consequences: the shell guard is the only boundary on a host without a sandbox, v0.9.1 is the last release with sandboxes, examples/harness is gone until agentkit-tools replaces it, and build-sandbox-containers.yaml stays in .github/workflows
   → the file opens with `# ADR 08: Leave sandboxes to the platform that runs them` and `- **Status:** Accepted`, and has the sections Context, Decision and Consequences, as ADRs 01 to 07 do
   Check: same as PATH-1
1. [REQ-5.2] THE ADR record SHALL keep ADR 05 and ADR 06 with their bodies unchanged and a status line saying each is superseded by ADR 08, with a link to it
   → each file's status line reads `- **Status:** Superseded by [ADR 08](08-leave-sandboxes-to-the-platform-that-runs-them.md)`; `git diff <base>` of each file changes that line only
   Check: same as PATH-1

## Execution Paths

### PATH-1: A maintainer checks the tree after the removal

1. **maintainer** runs `make check` at the root of the removal tree
2. **Makefile** runs fmt, vet, lint and the short tests in ., codesearch, mcpserve and examples/indexedsearch
3. **maintainer** runs `make doc` and `make tidy`, then `make help` and `make proto`
4. **git** reports the working tree unchanged and lists no tracked file under the removed trees
5. **maintainer** searches the docs, the doc comments and every go.mod for the names of the removed module, and reads ADR 05, 06 and 08

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** Makefile, go toolchain, golangci-lint, git, the repository's docs and go.mod files

**Setup:**

- a checkout of the removal branch with the v0.9.1 tags fetched, and <base> the commit the branch starts from
- provider credentials scrubbed from the environment (env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -u OPENROUTER_API_KEY), as for any run of the tests

**End state:**

- make check exits 0, having run in exactly the four modules MODULES lists
- `make doc` and `make tidy` leave `git status --porcelain` empty, and docs/generated/ holds no sandbox/ directory
- `make help` lists no removed target and `make proto` fails with `No rule to make target`
- `git ls-files sandbox containers/agentkit-sandbox examples/sandbox examples/gateway examples/harness .dockerignore` prints nothing and .gitignore has no /agentkit-sandboxd line
- `go list -m all` in each module lists neither rsync nor go-landlock, and every go.mod line naming grpc or protobuf ends in `// indirect`
- `git diff --stat <base> -- .github/workflows` prints nothing
- the search of REQ-4.1's files and REQ-4.4's comments for the removed names matches only docs/releasing.md's statement of the last release with sandboxes; docs/DEPS.md names none of the four removed dependencies; docs/cli.md is its title and one line
- docs/adr/08-leave-sandboxes-to-the-platform-that-runs-them.md exists with status Accepted, and ADR 05 and ADR 06 differ from <base> only in a status line pointing to it

**Pseudocode:**

```
a shell session, not a committed test (steering forbids tests of artefacts): `env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -u OPENROUTER_API_KEY make check`; assert exit 0 and that its `go test -short ./... (<m>)` lines name exactly the four modules; `make doc && make tidy && git status --porcelain` is empty; `make help | grep -Ei 'sandbox|gateway|container|proto'` is empty; `make proto` exits non-zero; `git ls-files <removed paths>` is empty; for m in the four modules: `(cd $m && go list -m all) | grep -E 'gokrazy/rsync|go-landlock'` is empty; `grep -hE 'google.golang.org/(grpc|protobuf) ' $(git ls-files '*go.mod') | grep -v '// indirect'` is empty; `git diff --stat <base> -- .github/workflows` is empty; `grep -niE 'agentkit-sandboxd|agentkit-gateway|gatewayd|landlock|podman|sandbox/' <REQ-4.1 docs> <REQ-4.4 files>` and `grep -nE 'sandbox\.[A-Z]' <the same files>` match only the releasing.md statement, so prose such as 'not a sandbox.' is not a match; `git diff <base> -- docs/adr/05-* docs/adr/06-*` changes one status line each
```

### PATH-2: A pinned consumer finds the last release with sandboxes

1. **consumer** reads docs/releasing.md and finds v0.9.1 named as the last release with sandboxes
2. **consumer** resolves sandbox/v0.9.1 with git
3. **git** shows the tagged tree, which holds sandbox/go.mod, on the commit the removal follows

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** git, the v0.9.1 tags, docs/releasing.md

**Setup:**

- a checkout of the removal branch with the tags fetched from origin (`git fetch --tags origin`), and <base> the commit the branch starts from

**End state:**

- docs/releasing.md names v0.9.1 as the last release with sandboxes and sandbox/v0.9.1 as the version to pin, and its tag commands name no sandbox/ tag
- v0.9.1, codesearch/v0.9.1, sandbox/v0.9.1 and mcpserve/v0.9.1 each resolve to <base>
- `git ls-tree --name-only sandbox/v0.9.1 -- sandbox/go.mod` prints sandbox/go.mod

**Pseudocode:**

```
a shell session: `grep -n 'sandbox/v0.9.1' docs/releasing.md` matches the statement; for t in v0.9.1 codesearch/v0.9.1 sandbox/v0.9.1 mcpserve/v0.9.1: assert `git rev-parse $t^{commit}` == <base>; assert `git ls-tree --name-only sandbox/v0.9.1 -- sandbox/go.mod` == 'sandbox/go.mod'
```

### 3. Record the decision in ADR 08 and mark ADR 05 and ADR 06 superseded (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-5

**Steps:**

- 3.1 Write docs/adr/08-leave-sandboxes-to-the-platform-that-runs-them.md in the shape of ADRs 01 to 07: the title line `# ADR 08: Leave sandboxes to the platform that runs them`, `- **Status:** Accepted`, today's date, then Context, Decision and Consequences
- 3.2 Context: AgentKit's own sandboxes (PRD 11, specs 13 to 19 and 25), about 15 000 lines of production Go, used inside the repository only by three examples; Parley now owns sandboxes on OpenShell; PRD 10's rule that the tools are kept because the model is bad at judgment and sandboxes only because AgentKit chose to own the whole stack
- 3.3 Decision: the sandbox module, the gateway, the sandbox image and their examples are deleted whole, in one cut, with no Landlock library kept; v0.9.1, with its codesearch/, sandbox/ and mcpserve/ tags, is the last release with sandboxes
- 3.4 Consequences: the shell guard is the only boundary on a host without a sandbox, as before PRD 11; a consumer pins sandbox/v0.9.1; examples/harness is gone until the agentkit-tools command replaces it; grpc and protobuf remain only as indirect requirements; build-sandbox-containers.yaml stays in .github/workflows by the owner's decision and fails until the owner changes it
- 3.5 In ADR 05 and ADR 06 replace the status line with `- **Status:** Superseded by [ADR 08](08-leave-sandboxes-to-the-platform-that-runs-them.md)` and change nothing else
